therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: melanoma risk reduction through improved photoprotective behaviors
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: families with children at risk for melanoma
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: percent of participants retained throughout intervention

results.target_engagement_evidence: Improved photoprotective behaviors including increased sunscreen use, protective clothing, and shade-seeking
biomarker_changes: Reduced melanin index values in children from baseline to follow-up
Decreased UV exposure measured by dosimeter from week 1 to week 9
subgroup_findings: Parents showed greater improvement in long-sleeve shirt wearing and long pants/skirt wearing
Children showed sustained improvements in protective clothing behaviors

results_by_chain.mechanism_description: behavioral education targeting family sun protection practices through structured intervention sessions
results_by_chain.biology_description: melanoma risk reduction through improved photoprotective behaviors in high-risk families
results_by_chain.population_description: families with children at elevated melanoma risk
